name: Curve DEX
rootCause: The Curve Finance frontend was attacked, prompting users to grant token approvals to malicious smart contracts. The attackers moved the stolen funds to FixedFloat and Tornado Cash, with at least 362 ETH (~$620,000) stolen. FixedFloat tweeted that they had frozen 112 stolen ETH (~$192,000).

descriptions.text: Curve fell victim to a DNS hijacking yesterday, with approximately $575k lost to malicious contract approvals. For users, DeFi protocols are only as secure as their centrally-hosted front end. How much longer will web3 rely on web2?

The Curve Finance frontend was attacked, prompting users to grant token approvals to malicious smart contracts. The attackers moved the stolen funds to FixedFloat and Tornado Cash, with at least 362 ETH (~$620,000) stolen. FixedFloat tweeted that they had frozen 112 stolen ETH (~$192,000).

On August 9, 2022, Curve Finance suffered a DNS hijack that redirected the main frontend, curve.fi, to an attacker-controlled clone. Users interacting with the site approved malicious token allowances, resulting in the theft of about $575,000 to $615,000, primarily in USDC and DAI. Curve's contracts were not breached. Rapid response included social media warnings, a switch to a backup domain, DNS restoration, and exchange intervention. An attacker compromised Curve Finance's domain registrar account, hijacked DNS settings for curve.fi, and redirected traffic to a malicious clone containing code to prompt wallet approvals for an attacker's contract.
